messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: GPU queue depth for prod-cluster has exceeded 9000 tokens across 12 pending requests. Autoscaler attempted 3 scaleups but node additions failed. Pager sent to oncall-night. https://internal.ops/incident/2923456789

maria: seeing the same in the console, queueing rate spiked after a big batch embed job. Pods in gpu-queue are Pending with "AttachVolume/AttachVolumeWaitExceeded" and a few show "FailedCreatePodSandBox".

aj: can you paste the pod events?

maria: sure, gist: 
```
kubectl -n inference describe pod gpu-req-7b9d
Events:
  Type     Reason             Age   From               Message
  ----     ------             ----  ----               -------
  Warning  FailedScheduling   3m    default-scheduler  0/10 nodes are available: 10 node(s) didn't match node affinity or selector.
  Normal   Scheduled          2m    kubelet            Successfully assigned inference/gpu-req-7b9d to ip-10-0-3-45.ec2.internal
  Warning  FailedCreatePodSandBox 2m kubelet            Failed to create pod sandbox: rpc error: code = Unknown desc = failed to set up network for sandbox
```

kevin: that network error might be a red herring. I'm seeing ASG attach profile failures in the autoscaler logs: `AttachRoleWithPolicy: AccessDenied` for the nodegroup role.

carla: confirmed in cloudtrail: `iam:PassRole` denied when the autoscaler tried to attach the launch template permissions to new instances. Looks like the instance-profile was recently rotated and missing the passrole for the autoscaler service account.

maria: ohhh. that would explain repeated failed node adds. queue keeps growing, latency for generation calls > 4s and token cost ballooning. We should assess customer impact now.

support-bot: CustomerImpactBot: 27 active customers with >95th percentile latency increases; 3 customers showing timeouts for streaming responses, two of which are in EU region. Ticket numbers created: INC-87421, INC-87422, INC-87423.

aj: mitigation options: (1) fix IAM/passrole so autoscaler can add nodes; (2) manually scale up nodegroup via console with privileged creds; (3) drain/shift some low-priority workloads to cpu-pool to free GPU queue; (4) toggle fallback routing to smaller quantized model on CPU to reduce GPU demand.

kevin: I can push a quick IAM patch: add `iam:PassRole` for `arn:aws:iam::123456:role/redwood-autoscaler` to the ops-runner role. Need 2 approvals for infra-iam. Who can +1?

carla: +1, this is safe and reversible.

maria: +1 from eng-sre, go ahead kevin.

kevin: applying now, will post commands.

kevin: running: 
```bash
aws iam attach-role-policy --role-name ops-runner --policy-arn arn:aws:iam::aws:policy/PassRoleForAutoscalerTemp
# policy created to grant PassRole to redwood-autoscaler
```

kevin: ok patch applied. Starting new scale attempts. Autoscaler log tail: 
```
2026-03-15T02:34:21Z INFO scaling: attempting scale up: want 3 -> 6
2026-03-15T02:34:27Z INFO provider/aws: create instance in nodegroup gpu-nodes-1
2026-03-15T02:35:12Z INFO provider/aws: instance i-0ab12c created, attaching LT v7
2026-03-15T02:35:45Z INFO kubelet: node ip-10-0-4-189 ready
```

maria: pods are scheduling, a few GPUs came up. queue depth dropped from 12 -> 4 in 6 minutes. latency back to ~600ms for most.

support-bot: CustomerImpactBot: Impact update: affected customer count decreased to 6, timeouts resolved for two EU customers. Notifying account reps.

aj: we should also enable short-term routing fallback to the CPU-bound quantized model for any new requests from low-tier keys until we finish verifying. Who controls routing config?

carla: that’s in the routing service. I can flip a canary route to send 30% of non-enterprise traffic to cpu-quantized-2 for the next 30 minutes.

maria: please do it, label it `temp-gpu-throttle-20260315`. Keep analytics enabled.

carla: done. config snippet: 
```json
{"route":"/v1/generate","policy":{"fraction":0.3,"selector":"tier!=enterprise","model":"cpu-quantized-2","ttl":"30m"}}
```

kevin: quick postmortem notes: root cause = recent instance-profile rotation removed PassRole permission for autoscaler service. Contributing factor = big scheduled embedding job without rate limits. Runbook gap = no automated alert for PassRole attach failures specific to autoscaler.

aj: actions: 
- create alert for `AttachRoleWithPolicy`/`PassRole` denies in cloudtrail -> pager.
- add a CI check for instance-profile rotations to verify autoscaler role mapping.
- run a throttling experiment to prevent single batch jobs from saturating GPU pool.

maria: also recommend we document manual recovery steps in the runbook: how to manually add node via console, how to attach the instance profile, and fallback routing steps.

oncall-night: handing off to daytime oncall (kevin) for verification and follow-up. I will stay available for 30m. Summary: autoscaler blocked by IAM PassRole after profile rotation, manual patch applied, nodes recovered, GPU queue drained, temporary routing enabled. Impact: transient latency spikes and a handful of timeouts, reduced to residual warnings.

kevin: taking handoff. I'll create the cloudtrail alert and start the CI check PR. Filing follow-up tickets: SRE-1198 (CloudTrail alert), SRE-1199 (CI verify rotation), SRE-1200 (Runbook docs).

maria: thx team. closing incident thread after postmortem note. :thumbsup:

support-bot: CustomerImpactBot: Final update: all customer timeouts resolved. Postmortem link: https://internal.reports/pm/2923456789
